title: RAG Security and Access Control: Visual Guide
outline: Title: RAG Security and Access Control - five interactive visuals on ACL-aware retrieval, tenant isolation and prompt injection via retrieved content.

1. Filter Or Boundary | The bridge from Metadata Filters in Context Assembly: three places to put the permission check - instruct the model, post-filter after the top-5, or pre-filter inside the index - over the same 10 scored chunks, of which the user may read 4. Shows which chunks are candidates, which are fetched, and what reaches the context. | Instructions are not access control: the context is the ceiling of what an answer can leak, and only an in-index pre-filter both prevents the breach and keeps the depth.

2. Post-Filter Starvation | Two sliders (eligibility rate p from 1-100%, fetch size n from 50-2000) plus a post-filter/pre-filter toggle, computing expected eligible yield n x p, the discarded work, and the fetch n >= k/p needed to hold rerank depth 50. | Post-filtering costs 1/p - at 5% eligibility you fetch 1,000 to keep 50 - and the observable result count is itself an existence oracle; pre-filtering removes p from the equation entirely.

3. The Isolation Ladder | Four rungs of tenant isolation (separate clusters, separate indexes, namespaces/partitions, tenant_id as an ordinary filter) crossed with four non-filter controls (cache keying, log scoping, tenant-scoped training data, response-layer re-verification), showing which of five leak channels stay OPEN. | A perfect tenant filter closes exactly one channel of five; cache, embeddings, logs and fine-tuning leak across tenants whatever the index looks like, so defense in depth plus a first-class tenant_id is the answer.

4. The Poisoned Ticket | A five-stage stepper through the indirect prompt injection narrative - the competitor's 400-day refund ticket, its ingest, the customer's genuine question, the retriever surfacing it correctly, and the generator repeating it with a laundered citation - checking each stage for a malfunction. | No stage malfunctioned: the failure is architectural, because untrusted content had an unfiltered path to the context and the model was trusted to be skeptical.

5. Blast Radius Control | Five togglable defense layers (sanitization, provenance labels, privilege separation, output controls, detection) recomputing which consequences a successful injection can still reach - act, exfiltrate, mislead, go unnoticed. | Probabilistic layers lower how often injection lands; only the structural ones cap what a landing can do, turning a breach into a wrong answer the evaluation layer can catch. No complete defense exists as of early 2026.
